body.input: REVIEW TEXT I used Chapala for my wedding in January 2026. They catered for over 100 people with everything I could want - tacos (pollo y asada), rice, beans, aguas frescas, and toppings for the tacos. They were responsive to email and then as the date got closer, we switched to texting. The total was due a week in advance and was amazingly affordable for the amount of food. The tacos were premade, ready to go in their tortillas, which kept the large line flowing at a good pace. The delivered to the venue in Mount Vernon, with no extra charge. Everyone raved about the food, saying that it was the best wedding food they have ever had. On top of all of that, Chapala staff was so nice through the whole process. I am so happy to have shared my favorite place with all my friends and family on my wedding day.

body.input: REVIEW TEXT First of all in an near empty dining room with many open tables we were sat in a table with the highest traffic. My seat was kicked at least four times and my wife was hit with two jackets and a purse during our meal. I did contest at the start and point at a lovely two top next to the window but was met with conjecture.   I stared at it empty until a little over half way through our meal.  Our meal.  I excitedly ordered the beef marrow bones, and brussel sprouts as the appetizer and my wife the steak salad medium rare, I the $60 new york also medium rare.  I often get rare due to the uncertainty of the kitchen but I was counting on the quality of the steakhouse.  The marrow bones and brussel sprouts.  I harvested a little more than half a teaspoon of marrow off the first bone plopped it on my crustini and looked around thinking it was a joke.  I had roasted garlic on the other crustini and went to the second bone to excitedly find a whole tablespoon of marrow to dollop on the other two crustini with more roasted garlic.  That was $20.  The brussel sprouts was a mushy pile of sweet mess.  My wife's salad came. She likes blue cheese crumbles but not blue cheese dressing. She substituted ranch still wanted the crumbles.  No crumbles. Steak was good medium rare as requested.   My steak arrived with a lite sear around the edges, charred broccoli on a sauce.  The steak was medium, toward the center was a sliver of medium rare.  Tough for an aged new york. After I was done with the grissel laden steak I commented that it was a bit dry and needed a bit of sauce and realized that it didn't have any of the signature burbon butter on my steak. They forgot it. I happend to see another steak go by with a big dollop on it.  The side dish of sweet potato came a minute or two after the mains were set, was luke warm in a sweet sour sauce that was unpleasant. This was not a good experience.

body.input: REVIEW TEXT I have been going to double barrel barbecue since they started out by the road on Riverside Drive at CTK. And I’ve followed them to the other locations they have had. REVIEW TEXT We stopped at Tacos Tecalitlan on our way back from Sedro-Woolley, and I’m really glad we did. What a great place. The food was excellent, the atmosphere was welcoming, and you can tell there’s a lot of pride behind what they do.

I learned that they originally operated out of just a taco truck, which honestly makes it even more impressive to see them now running a full-scale restaurant. That kind of growth doesn’t happen without consistently good food and community support, and it shows.

I ordered the quesabirria, and it absolutely did not disappoint. Rich, flavorful, perfectly cooked, and satisfying in that way where you’re already thinking about when you can come back for it again.
If you’re anywhere nearby, this spot is 100% worth the stop.

body.input:
REVIEW TEXT I’m a bit late in posting this, but my meal at Nonna Luisa last month was so memorable I had to make sure they got the credit they deserve.
From the moment I walked in, the atmosphere was perfect. They start you off with incredible bread and honestly, I could have just kept eating that all night and been happy. For the main course, I had a variation of spaghetti with sausage. It was something I’ve haven’t had in a long time, but it was savory, delicious, and easily some of the best pasta I’ve ever had.
What really sets this place apart is the service and the owner. He spends his time walking the floor and treating every guest like family, creating a truly authentic Italian experience. When I tried to speak a little Italian when I walked in and froze up, he was incredibly kind and patient. That level of genuine hospitality is rare. Leaving was just as pleasant as arriving, complete with a handshake and a sincere thank you.
If you want amazing food and a place where you feel genuinely welcome, this is it. I won't forget the kindness or the meal!

body.input: REVIEW TEXT We had high hopes for this awesome space.   Very well designed, with a fireplace and lots of natural wood surfaces...soooo inviting, comfortable and cozy!   The menu has a nice variety of regular fare and a few specialty items.  The prime rib sandwich caught the eye of two of us.  I have a soft spot for prime rib roast beef and especially in the form of a dip sandwich.  Unfortunately the meat was tough, dry and suspiciously not prime...probably round or regular roast beef.  And on top of not being prime, it was overcooked and not hot.   AND it was a very small $23 sandwich.   So there is that.   The pork enchiladas with a wonderful green sauce were outstanding.  The portion, again, was on the small side, more like an appetizer portion.  It is a brew pub and there was no non-alcoholic beer on tap.   We thought that a bit odd.  They did have Athletic N/A beer in a can, and it was fine.  Service was very decent,  decor and architecture was the stand out feature of this brew pub.  We wanted to like it more, but will probably not be back.  And, if it was prime rib, they managed to degrade it to questionable cut status.  Prime rib should absolutely have at least a hint of pink (rare or medium rare meat).  I hope they can take this review in the spirit in which it is submitted....., regroup, correct and try again.  Please up your game folks.

body.input: REVIEW TEXT Gross! Disclosure, I am a chef but I appreciate down to earth Americanized Chinese food. Although I look for authentic when I can get it. But I could definitely make 10 times better food than this without trying. Unfortunately I was on a medical overnight stay to make my commute to the hospital easier. I was looking to just have a nice treat in my room before I cozied up and watched some TV. Disappointing to say the least. Also very expensive for the portions. I also found the owner's response. Very annoying. Yes, I am well versed in Cantonese Mandarin Szechuan Korean Vietnamese cuisines. I was trained by Hong Kong chefs and have over 16 years of schooling and 40 years in restaurant service, owned three restaurants and am still executive chef and food and beverage manager of a golf and country club. So yes, I have enough education to tell you that your food is trash. And instead of just apologizing, you chose to weirdly defend your mediocre to poor skills while making excuses forgiving less than adequate size value. For your price. I get it. The restaurant business is hard. Maybe you just had an off night but don't put it on me. Probably not a great idea to fight over social media.

I am sorry to say I will probably not be back here for a very long time. When this place lacked in expeditious service, they made up for a great food quality. However, they lack both now.

REVIEW TEXT A bunch of gluten-free sandwiches -- unfortunately, their GF bread is MEH!  I ordered a Calico Cuban.  What I got was a bit of pulled pork, a bacon slice, some condiments, and dab of apparently undrained coleslaw.  The sandwich was bland and so soggy (the rice-flour based GF bread?) that it was a knife & fork affair.  Definitely not appetizing nor tasty At nearly $22 (including a huge upcharge for the GF bread), wholly disappointing.  This review was saved by my travel partner's pastrami sandwich, which she enjoyed. (And was also nearly $20).

Disappointing, expensive food means no more returns (and this is after we used to eat there on a semi-regular basis while living in the area).

I normally believe in second chances - however, not when two sandwiches, no drinks other than water, and a nice tip brings a mediocre lunch bill to over $56.

body.input: REVIEW TEXT We arrived for our reserved time at Nell Thorn Restaurant.  We were greeted nicely and seated right away. Great so far. Our waitress bopped up to our table after a long wait. We ordered wine and placed our dinner order. The wine arrived 15 minutes later, the restaurant was not crowded at all. Our salad was delivered after another long wait but not our appetizer.  The gentleman who delivered our salad was very nice and when we asked about our appetizer, he looked confused and says that he will check. Five minutes later our waitress bopped up again and literally said, “my bad” and do we still want our appetizer? We said no. She came back later and offered us a free dessert. We picked crème brûlée. It arrived and the crust was really thick and hard. We took a bite and the crème was thin and grainy in texture. Our entree was really good as was our wine. The experience though was a complete disappointment.

REVIEW TEXT We chose this restaurant to celebrate our 15th wedding anniversary—our first time ever splurging on an upscale anniversary dinner. I noted the anniversary on the reservation, and at check-in there was a noticeable change in the host’s demeanor after she realized we were a lesbian couple.

From that point on, the evening felt cold and unwelcoming. Our anniversary was never acknowledged, and when we left, the host was rude to my wife. While the food was excellent, hospitality is about more than what’s on the plate.

At our age, it’s rare to experience this kind of treatment anymore, which made it especially disappointing—particularly from a restaurant that presents itself as refined and inclusive. We won’t be returning.

I was in Arlington to perform on a comedy show with my bestie Cheri Hardman and we drove even further north just to come here before heading back to Tacoma. And boy was I glad she suggested it.

First of all the decor and atmosphere are exactly what you want from a classic ice cream parlor. Everything from the red and white checked floors, the heart-backed chairs, to the lighting, were all the exact touches to set the tone. Then of course the staff, super friendly and helpful.

Now for the tastiest part... ice cream and food. That's the way we ordered it too. Ice cream first so we didn't run out of room.

There is a long case of every flavor of ice cream you could want at the counter, plus their full menu of sundaes and desserts to choose from. I of course had to go for the one with hot fudge and butterscotch in the same dish. While Cheri's was a hot fudge and banana dish.

Once the main course was over (dessert) we got to our sandwiches. My club sandwich was great with the perfect fries on the side. Plus I stole one of Cheri's onion rings just so I could tell you how great they are!

Drive out of your way to come here, you won't be sorry.

PS I didn't know Cheri was taking my picture while I snapped a pic for this review so you get a rare behind the scenes view. 😅

REVIEW TEXT I very rarely post a review, and usually when I get home, but I have to write this as I sit in the cafe. This was one of the best sandwiches I've had in my life. I got the spicy pork, and I can confidently say I've had sandwiches that were twice the price that this one blows out of the water. I'm always on the hunt for a great sandwich and this place hit the nail on the head. I'm so mad I live an hour away because I would be here every day. The service was quick even with only one guy working here. I also got the sweet potato croquettes which were delicious but the sandwich was the real star.
The only negative comment I have is their coffee is sort of so-so. It's not bad but I think I'll have a lemonade next time. I can also recognize I may have caught them on an off day with it. I'm also picky about coffee, so maybe it's just me.
Overall a 5/5 experience, I will be back.

body.input:
REVIEW TEXT I ordered directly through their website for delivery. I did not receive my full order. Katie was VERY rude and aggressive on the phone when I kindly called to sort it out and see what could be done.The first person was very kind but needed to get assistance. I was handed off to Katie who was extremely rude and not professional. She continued to try to rush me off of the phone when I had questions.
I paid a delivery fee and tipped my driver. I understand that they are using a third party delivering company these things happen. I am just baffled at the way that Katie handled this. I get it if there are certain rules, it's a bummer that they were requiring me to come to the store when I was at work and got it delivered for that specific reason.
She had a very condescending and annoyed tone. She even snapped at me several times. I was not being irrational, rude or any of that nonsense. I was very kind as I also work in customer service so I always try to be kind to those I'm interacting with. I understand that it can get busy. However, if it's too busy to handle a phone call, maybe let it ring or place them on hold instead of answering the phone when slammed and then being absolutely rude.

Food is generally good and accurate. But the way that this was handled with lack of professionalism, the lack of common courtesy, consideration and kindness was really frustrating. I had to remove stars based on customer service from this experience.

REVIEW TEXT Nice atmosphere. The bagel had reasonably good bones. But coming out of the toaster there was zero crisp, just a bit warm. Cream cheese quantity is better than Starbucks but not awesome like in NYC.
What frustrated me a bit was ordering a sesame bagel that by the time it was served had like 5 sesame seeds left on it. It was by appearance and flavor now a plain bagel. When I asked about it, the shedding of seeds was blamed on the toaster. What the what? While I don’t doubt this to have been true… it should never be true.

I’ll include a stock photo vs my bagel.

My family is from NY and my dad raised me on bagels… I admit to being a bagel snob, but this issue of bagels being denuded of seeds by the toaster would be a great matter to sort out.

Wishing all success.

REVIEW TEXT We ordered a beef and lamb gyro, a chicken shawarma and a Greek salad. Portions are large, so you can make a meal out of one of these. Quality wise, it's top notch. Probably some of the better gyros I've had in western Washington and outside of Europe! We particularly liked the sauces they used; they taste homemade.

We ordered around 6, and they were slammed, so expect about 5-10 minutes longer than the online estimate during dinner. It's also kind of a small space, so not the best place to dine in if you're a larger group.

Overall, Mt. Vernon has been needing a good Greek restaurant for ages, so I'm really glad we finally got one. I'll definitely be eating here all the time.

body.input:
REVIEW TEXT Rachel's Alibi is an absolute gem! From the moment you walk in and seat yourself, the warm and friendly staff make you feel right at home. The service is impressively quick, and the food is hearty and delicious. It’s no wonder this spot is a favorite among the locals.

Every dish is prepared with fresh, high-quality ingredients, offering a wonderful balance of taste and comfort. The BBQ boneless chicken wings are a standout—tender, well-seasoned, and some of the best I’ve ever had. For burger enthusiasts, the smash burgers are a must-try; making it a double is absolutely highly recommended. The tomato bisque is rich and satisfying, perfect for a cozy meal on a cold day.

Rachel’s Alibi is wonderfully family-friendly, and even our teenagers gave it a big thumbs-up. It’s the kind of place you’ll want to visit again and again for an enjoyable, laid-back home style dining experience.

Of note, there are larger booths available for bigger groups, as well as counter service for those looking to grab a quick lunch.

body.input:
REVIEW TEXT I was likely the first person of the day to dine with you, and the coffee and food were great!

Unfortunately a smell I have seen mentioned in a couple of posts was strong and almost unbearable at 7:15AM.  (It wasn't me, I checked...) Perhaps it was the the bathroom,  bleach, the carpet, or a combination of both?

I imagine when the place is full it is less noticeable.  Yet because 75-95% of taste is smell, and bad smells unconsciously make people annoyed, I suggest checking this out and perhaps adding some smell diffusers.  You could even go full "Disney Park" and get machines that pump out a rich diner smell!

I suspect you will get many more 5 star reviews, not to mention it will be easier to keep staff.  I have had complaints about employers in the past but didn't say them because I need my job, right?

Please don't take my word for it though. This is intended as constructive criticism.  Perhaps bring three trusted friends who are not accustomed to the place in the early morning as an independent assessment.

The food was great!  I'll come back in a month or so to try it again, and I am certainly open to editing this review.  Good luck!

REVIEW TEXT This was my first visit to this restaurant...

The smothered burrito was fabulous (needless to say I had leftovers 😳) and the halibut fish and chips were cooked to perfection! Portions were ample. Also indulged in a piece of chocolate pie and a chocolate chip cookie.

Service was exceptional and wait time was minimal. Prices were surprisingly lower than expected.

Restaurant opens early (6:30am) making it a wonderful spot to have breakfast; however, was thrilled to learn the rather extensive breakfast menu is available all day, every day.

Such a cute restaurant with easy access and only a few miles from Deception Pass.

I highly recommend and will personally be back several times as I work my way through the menu.

Open one in Oregon City, Oregon, please!

REVIEW TEXT EDIT - I've been going back, and it seems like my review was an isolated incident because the food and service have been pretty dang good! My only complaint would be the smell by the front door. There was a musty smell as we walked in and smelled it had gotten wet, maybe the carpet. However, our breakfasts and service were good, and we will keep going back.

We were really looking forward to trying this place as we literally live behind it! So first of all the coffee is fenominal ! Like I'm not a coffee drinker and would drink this coffee every day.  Tony's out Bellingham if you're curious. We went in hungry 😋 the waitress was nice enough but we got someone else's breakfast and again we were hungry so good thing we didn't just start eating. After some confusion and the waitress checking how she made this mistake, she realized it was someone else's order. Then our order came out and looked good enough, but as I cut into the eggs, I realized they were still raw, and the whites were still clear and stringy at this point my patients is gone and I'm feeling like my meal was a bust and for 47$( with tip) for 2 breakfasts I would be hesitant to try it again. After all that, I might have comped the coffee or something, but no such luck. I hate giving a bad review, but this was our experience, and it wasn't great.

body.input:
REVIEW TEXT Every year, in November, I join friends and family for a trip to a secret location in the San Juan Islands. The adventure starts in the dark, with a drive up to Anacortes to catch a ferry to Friday Harbor. This year, the weather was cold and rainy. We had a 20 minute wait in line - just enough time for a latte. The bad news was that the coffee in the ferry terminal is terrible. Still, it was hot, so we reluctantly headed in. That was when my daughter spotted Dockside - a mobile booth set up next to the holding area. We made an immediate course correction.
There was fruit in baskets out front, all the usual coffee add-ons on a counter and a window where an enthusiastic barista greeted us. He bantered his way through taking our orders and assured us that we would have our drinks in (Checks the order list) "Three minutes and twenty eight seconds."
I did not time him, but it was not long before I had my hands warming around a latte that tasted great. Several of the people we would meet on the boat to our secret location joined us to catch up on personal news and drink coffee. Before we knew it, the tannoy blared the announcement that it was time to load. What a great way to pass the time.
I have a few more trips planned this Winter and I am looking forward to the Dockside part of those trips.

REVIEW TEXT Plant based, gluten free, local, mostly organic, good for the planet. A great place to come to feed and nourish your body. A huge variety of smoothies and juices with natural sweetners like banana/fruit, honey, or dates instead of sugar or high fructose corn syrup.

I got the tofu sandwich with came with plenty of fresh veggies like lettuce, roasted peppers, cucumber, onions, Sprouts, hummus on a toasted sourdough bread with rippled potato chips. I got the 16 oz Golden Milk smoothie as well. It was plenty for dinner and I didn't feel weighed down afterwards but lighter and more peppy.

I got my food to go, but there were some Bistro tables inside and children's artwork on the walls.

body.input:
REVIEW TEXT The opposite of "Fast Food!"

Don’t get me wrong; the service here is quick, friendly, and attentive. But the food? It’s on another level. Thoughtfully prepared, gloriously fresh, and packed with nutrition, every bite feels like it’s doing your body a favor. It’s hearty, satisfying, and far better value than most salads in A-Town.

The shop itself is clean and cozy, with a team that clearly cares about what they’re serving. If you’re looking for a wholesome alternative to the usual drive-thru fare, this place is a must.

I am not vegan, vegetarian, or even restricted (gluten, lactose, whatever...) This has not stopped me from appreciating this great food. Everyone should try it, you may love it, you know I do!

REVIEW TEXT We recently had the pleasure of working with Cosmic Veggies for a large order of 21 to-go meals, and we couldn't be more impressed! From start to finish, their team, led by the incredible Elizabeth, was responsive, accommodating, and downright delightful to work with.

Despite the challenge of fulfilling such a large order in a small kitchen, the Cosmic Veggies crew handled everything with efficiency and grace. They not only met our high expectations but exceeded them, delivering each order with precision and care. The quality of the food was exceptional—each meal was packed with flavor, freshness, and creativity. Our team was raving about the deliciousness of every bite!

What truly set this experience apart was their generosity and willingness to go above and beyond. When we arrived to pick up the orders, the team didn’t hesitate to help us load everything into our vehicle, ensuring we were well taken care of from start to finish.

Working with Elizabeth was a joy. Her professionalism and passion for what she does were evident throughout the entire process, making our collaboration smooth and enjoyable. We can't thank Cosmic Veggies enough for their incredible service and scrumptious food. We’ll definitely be returning for more!

REVIEW TEXT ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️
Consistently great, genuinely family-run. I’ve been coming to Real Tequila in Anacortes for years and love that it’s truly family operated—you see the same friendly faces every visit, and sometimes the kids pitching in midday, refilling waters and helping clear plates. The manager always stops by to say hello and make sure we have everything we need, and the servers are attentive without hovering. The food is delicious and consistent, with portions that feel just right. As a local, it’s my go-to Mexican spot because I always know what to expect: warm service, a welcoming atmosphere, and reliably tasty plates. Thanks to the whole team for always making us feel seen and taken care of.

body.input:
REVIEW TEXT I visited Anchor Inn after working an all-nighter and walking around to decompress. I ordered a martini, some wings, and then asked for a beer. Despite being calm, quiet, and clearly not slurring my words, the bartender cut me off—while patrons next to me were actively pounding shots and beers.

I understand that after 24 hours awake, I may have looked fatigued, but I wasn’t intoxicated. I even recorded myself afterward to verify I wasn’t slurring. What disappointed me most wasn’t being cut off—it was the lack of concern or basic human decency. No offer of water. No, “Hey man, you doing alright?”

Instead, the interaction felt like a public power move. If you’re from out of town and not fully adjusted to the time zone, think twice. And if you’re an attractive woman? I saw a visibly drunk regular grab a woman by the hips—no one said a word.

Maybe this place works for some locals, but between the selective enforcement and lack of care, I won’t be back.

REVIEW TEXT We wanted to play pool and decided to grab a bite to eat. From the start, the service was terrible!  And there was only one other person in the place. The bartender barely acknowledged us. We ordered the fish & chips. They were under-cooked (Unsafe by food handling requirements) and greasy. We couldn’t eat them. The general indoor air was smoke filled from the fryer in the kitchen.

We stayed long enough to play 3 games of pool. We had to approach the bartender for drink refills each time. We even had to come to the bar to get our credit card slip. We only received merchant copy and no customer copy or itemized bill). She did however come over right as we were completing tip and signing credit card slip. Which we left on table with our empties. As we were walking out she asked where credit card slip was like we were running out wthout paying. Yes we made her go to the table and get the signed credit card slip.
Emily is callous, rude and I have to say, lazy. We won’t be back. Terrible experience.

body.input:
REVIEW TEXT Disappointing hospitality during a much-needed stop

My husband and I were on a motorcycle trip from North Vancouver to Fidalgo Island, and we were excited to find Moka Joe Coffee House as a cozy-looking spot to rest and recharge.

Before ordering, we simply asked to use the restroom after a long journey, but were told we could only have the key after placing an order. This felt surprisingly unwelcoming especially in such a quiet location where one might expect a bit more hospitality. As world travelers who have been on the road for over 60,000 km, this is not something we’ve encountered even in busier, high-traffic areas.

We left disappointed, as this policy and the way it was communicated felt disrespectful. I hope the management considers a more flexible, friendly approach toward travelers and visitors in the future.

body.input:
REVIEW TEXT Look, I am a huge fan of Chipotle and I actually own Chipotle stock; so, I eat there to also support my investment...

HOWEVER...

I have noticed at several restaurants now that there is a growing amount of slovenliness going on that is not being addressed quickly and orderly...

For example, at the Anacortes WA Chipotle, I have noticed quite a bit of grunginess around the tray return area (food and trash on the floor and tray return area, tabletops clearly not cleaned and grungy, etc).  I have noted this on several occasions now and, as an investor, I really do not like to see this.  I have also witnessed this at several other Chipotle's in the Seattle area.

You dont see this kind of slovenliness in top notch fast food places like McDonald's...the restaurants are usually spic n span and any slovenliness/grunginess is removed quickly (I am sure there are some severe outliers).

If I were in corporate Chipotle, I would be making a company wide mandate to enforce more attention to keeping things clean and tidy promptly (by holding the Managers at each location responsible to delegate a small percentage of each worker's time dedicated to routine pickup/cleanup of the customer areas).

A bad customer experience can change the success of a business quickly.  I want Chipotle to be successful for decades to come... not just a few more years.

REVIEW TEXT The young woman helping us was kind, but wasn’t helpful when we asked questions regarding food, along with pricing on items since they weren’t shown on the menu! No idea how much we payed for everything but the total seemed fine.

My honest review, thank you Nations Coffee!

REVIEW TEXT I went to check out Sweet Corner a couple days ago and was pleasantly surprised by the experience! I ordered the brown sugar milk tea and enjoyed the tea. I got 100% sweetness and although I prefer sweeter drinks I might recommend a lower sugar level to others. The drink was sweet, flavorful, and I could taste the real tea inside. The tapioca was a bit inconsistent in terms of texture, as some pearls were more or less chewy than others. In that regard the tapioca was a bit disappointing but definitely not bad. The decor could use some work but they are also newly opened.
Overall, I was impressed as a boba enthusiast and quite pleased to finally have a boba shop in town!

body.input:
REVIEW TEXT DO NOT WASTE YOUR MONEY HERE!!

I ordered chicken fried rice, for $15.99 the portion should be adequate, but it wasn’t! Flavor was the most bland I’ve ever had in my life. How difficult is it to make chicken fried rice?! I cook it better at home!

They take the chicken from the teriyaki chicken they sell that still has the teriyaki sauce on it and cut it up and throw it into this overpriced garbage!!!!

To top it all off I asked for Sriracha and the rude despicable guy at the front counter lied and said they don’t have it. When I literally pointed to it, it must’ve struck a nerve in his feelings because he got even more irritated than he was initially when he took my order. He got all flustered and was walking back and forth and then proceeded to say it would be $1.00!! For a 15ml container of sauce. He clearly made that up because he was mad I called him out!

At this point I had enough and just left.

These crooks just wanna nickel and dime you from the get go!

OVERPRICED GARBAGE!!! I WOULDN’T FEED THIS CRAP TO MY WORST ENEMY!

There are better Asian restaurants in Anacortes, spend your hard earned money elsewhere in these hard expensive times.

body.input:
REVIEW TEXT I really wanted crab for Thanksgiving. Having had no luck in preparing the perfect turkey, ham, or prime rib I needed something different. I contacted Pacific Dram Seafoods to see if they were shipping to arrive the Wed before Thanksgiving and they said yes.

It was cheaper to order directly through them rather than on Amazon. I ordered the 8 pound box. And then waited, rather impatiently, for Wed to arrive.

My box arrived Wed morning, with 4 beautiful crabs that were still on ice and alive. They looked beautiful, just amazing. We added some additional cold pack because we were cooking them on Thursday. I know their site says to cook them the day they arrived, but we waited.

On Thanksgiving, we had 2 pots boiling with crab boil seasoning packets in them. Then gently lowered the crab into the pots, boiled them for 5 minutes, then let them sit in the hot water for an additional 20 minutes.

The crab came out perfect! Yea for us we finally had a great Thanksgiving dinner. The crab was so sweet and flavorful, the texture was perfect and no one ate the sides because we were so full from the crab. Oh well, corn & potatoes are good the next day.

My entire experience with Pacific Dream Seafoods was one of the best main dish experience from online order. I would definitely recommend them over any other seafood delivery service.

body.input: REVIEW TEXT i love Manchu Wok and figured I'd give Fatburger a try, well I am glad I did as I am beyond impressed. I got the XXXL Fatburger with bacon added, total came out to $21.34. now that may seem a little costly for a burger, but not this burger trust me...IT IS GIANT!! The beef is high quality, the grill taste is on point, the seasoning is pronounced, and the vegetables are fresh. I can devour a Wendy's triple burger and not even feel full, but half of this burger and I am SLAMMED and thats after fasting the whole day. Pleasantly surprised at how amazing Fatburger is and will continue to take on the heavenly XXXL behemoth for the foreseeable future! incredible burger, the lady who took my order was friendly, and I give atmosphere 3 stars because it is in a casino and  as an ex-employee of a casino I have seen gambling addiction firsthand and it can be very sad.

body.input: REVIEW TEXT The food was good, plates were big and loaded, I liked the appatizer- hubby did not.  My enchilada didn't seem cooked all the way,  I left most of it but the rice was good. We were the only ones in restaurant- they had music playing, but when we sat down, they shut it off and had it going in the back room.  When we asked for coffee, they only had instant as an option, so we had tea instead - we were left alone for the most part.  They did start music up again near end of meal but also put in a soccer game which competed with the music.  I think if they were busier it would have been different.

REVIEW TEXT *Update: ordered 1 year later, just as good as the first time, and we had more mouths to feed. Not only was there ample food, everything was tasty and fresh, everyone enjoyed the meal. We had 6 people and had tons of leftovers. Highly recommend!

Ordered takeout. Everything was packaged well, they included all utensils (even a spatula), Parmesan, mint chocolates, napkins, making serving a breeze! We were pleasantly surprised how piping hot the food was.

I’d heard nothing but great things about Olive Garden’s lasagna, and now having tried it, I understand why! We ordered a “small” and there was a lot of food. Depending who’s eating, it could feed 4-6 people.

•Lasagna 5/5: full to the brim, not overloaded with cheese or meat. Extremely well-seasoned, everything was equally distributed. Excellent flavor, as good as homemade, but without the hassle of cooking all day. I love how it wasn’t too salty or oily. I imagine this would be a hit for many since it isn’t spicy.

REVIEW TEXT I keep holding out hope for the day the dishes are as good as i remember.... but the food keeps falling short. I used to get fettuccine alfredo with grilled chicken, the chicken parmigiano, or the spaghetti with meatballs and each time the sauce is watery, the meat is weakly seasoned and rubbery, and anything that's not fried or steamed has a disappointing amount of flavor.

For likely my last time ordering from *this location* if not all olive gardens, I got a CYOP: rotini, mushroom cream sauce (not alfredo?), chicken fritta, and steamed broccoli. The broccoli was good, the chicken fritta as tasty, but the sauce was mostly water and there were like 4 slices of mushrooms in the sauce. The rotini was a weird offwhite color. The breadsticks were over-salted. Overall I'm not happy with the last 4 times I've eaten at OG. :(. super sad because there's no other Italian places in the area.

The Toasted Ravioli is great though.

REVIEW TEXT Always a go-to spot for delicious Italian comfort food. As a popular chain with multiple locations, it consistently delivers on flavor and service.

Dishes tried: Garden Salad, Zuppa Toscana Soup, Crispy Chicken Pasta, Grilled Chicken, Herb-Grilled Salmon, Marinara Pasta, Sicilian Cheesecake.

Review:
•	The Garden Salad is a classic favorite—fresh, crisp, and elevated by their signature dressing (which you can even find in some supermarkets!).
•	The Zuppa Toscana was rich and creamy, with hearty Italian sausage—definitely a must-try.
•	I built my own pasta with spaghetti, five cheese sauce, and crispy chicken, and it turned out to be a delicious combination—highly recommend for those customizing their meal.
•	The Grilled Chicken was cooked to perfection—juicy and flavorful.
•	The Herb-Grilled Salmon, however, was slightly overcooked and could have used a bit more finesse.
•	The meal ended on a high note with the Sicilian Cheesecake, which was hands down one of the best I’ve ever had—smooth, rich, and indulgent.

Service was impressively quick, with the added bonus of unlimited refills on salad, soup, and breadsticks. The ambience is simple and pleasant—nothing extravagant, but comfortably inviting.

Verdict: A reliable choice for satisfying, hearty Italian food. I’ll definitely be coming back for more.

REVIEW TEXT I’ve never written a bad review before  I’ve never even felt the need to  but today’s experience deserves it. I spent nearly $40 on three sandwiches, and every single one of them was made with the stingiest portions I’ve ever seen. The employee acted like the toppings were coming out of his own paycheck.

When I ordered a Subway Club, he didn’t know what was on it, made the wrong sandwiches, and only put mayo on half of one. When we asked for pickles, he added two slices total. I also asked for vinegar and he barely put any at all. On top of that, he spoke so quietly that I had to keep guessing what he was saying, and the whole interaction just felt uncomfortable and frustrating.

For the price I paid, the service and food quality were incredibly disappointing. This was honestly one of the worst experiences I’ve had at a Subway, and I left feeling like my money was completely wasted.

REVIEW TEXT My family and I have ordered lots of times but our last order was not good at all. We had ordered 2 order meals and 2 sides of 5 wings each.  First they combined everything together instead of putting the orders that were originally ordered. So with each family member we had to separate each out like we ordered. One order was 10 of one flavor and 5 of one and 5 of another flavor. They should have been in the box as ordered but they put all of one flavor in a box and another flavor in another box. So we had to totally separate each one out. Then flavors were not all correct and some of the flavors had not enough sauce to cover the wing. They said they would replace 1 of the meals and replace 10 of one flavor and 5 of another. I just now called to actually have it remade and they say they have to call me back in 20 min even though he read the whole order back to me. This is not good customer service and I know they get busy but when they say they will replace they say they will call me back. One picture was taken after we separated one and put in the other box.  When someone pays $50 for a meal you would expect it to be decent

This place is getting worse .

REVIEW TEXT I'd heard many good things about MOD Pizza, but this was our first time here. The create-your-own pizza pie concept was pretty cool. The fresh dough and vast fresh topping options were a nice change from the long established conventional pizza joints.

The atmosphere was sort of "industrial-loft-hipster", I guess, is as good a description as I can think of; it was cool, but not exactly comfortable as all seats were hard flat wooden slabs and cold steel. It was also a very loud space; not from people, but movement of the metal seats/stools and the kitchen equipment echoing around the concrete floor and corrugated steel walls.

The pizza pies were good sized for individuals and, as mentioned, everything was fresh. I thought, however, that the crust didn't taste that great and the sauce was bland. I went with one of their menu items, but wished I'd added other toppings to get more flavor, once I took a few bites. I will have to try it again and play around with my topping choices and re-evaluate. But for the most part, we were satisfied. Definitely a healthier option than other places.

body.input:
REVIEW TEXT TLDR: finally a Taste of India that is legitimately a taste of India.

We came here for dinner on the way to the Cascades - I had my reservations about how good it would be because of how picky I am about India food. Safe to say, this place really does do a fantastic job.

We ordered the paneer tikka masala, Baingan bharta, paratha and the coffee ice cream. Everything was fabulous. The baingan bharta was actually smoked and you could taste it - 💯

The coffee ice cream was really the highlight for me though (so much so that we came back the next day on our way back from the cascades, lol). It’s homemade and uses South Indian style coffee (with chicory!)

I’m very pleased with my experience here.
I will say, we ordered a spice level 4 and I think it overwhelmed the other flavors. I would recommend sticking with a level 3.

REVIEW TEXT I gave them a 3 for the menu board being very misleading.  Who has small print on a fast food drive thru? Carl's Jr does, it shows a burger and says combo then the price which tells me that burger in a combo is the displayed price except wait nope it's the burger price says so in small print nobys can see.  I guess the word combo is just a suggestion of what you should get with the  10.39 burger.  There was 3 people in my vehicle and we all read it the same way. Whoever is in charge of advertisement should really try an honest approach I'm sure your making money on your current plan but not long term cause people like me (honest) people don't appreciate being mislead, being switched up on them, we want what we thought we were agreeing to when we ordered not get knocked out with a total that is 20 bucks then you had planned just 10 seconds earlier. Not all of us have a endless supply of money especially this time of the year.  I will not return to this restaurant until they change that aspect of their menu. I work to hard to get my money so I'm not willing to add $20 over fine print.
The kid in the drive through was a good, polite, and overall provided great customer service. This was drive thru in Mount veron, Wa about 9:45pm

body.input: REVIEW TEXT I haven’t been back here in 2 1/2 years, and the service was incredible today. Our server miss Jenn was incredibly helpful and fast as well as friendly. The atmosphere is very welcoming as well and the temperature inside is nice and cool on a hot summer day such as today. Our experience here today was the best we had in years and the staff was incredible. The chefs in the back deserve a thanks for making the single best burger I have had in years from this establishment. I highly recommend coming here and I am glad to say I will be a returning customer!

REVIEW TEXT I ordered chili and got a "modified" chili recipe - no burger meat included.  When, I compained to the manager she asked me to return the chili I was unhappy with.  I attempted to hand it to her in the the bag and she refused to accept it.  She claimed the recipe was unchanged.  "Good luck Wendy's"!  Your chili was totally unsatisfactory, today. She tried to justify Wendy's policy by comparing it to Walmarts policy;  I needed to present un-satisfactory, un-eaten product to demonstrate my dis-satisfaction.  Are you serious?

I have been a Wendy's, Inc. Stock holder in the past.  Recently, I have read that 100's of Wendy's locations are closing.  Now, after my experience today, I have a solid idea why Wendy's is failing.  You have lost a customer for life.

For people who do not live at the building, the parking is going to be rather difficult. But even so I greatly suggest supporting this new location.

I come here and get the exact same thing, yet I get enough ice to fill a pounder glass halfway. Will not go back and stick to the main store where they listen. I got a 16 oz for the price of a 24oz. Yes i put it in a 16oz cup and fit perfectly, and i have yet to drink any. The last pick before the cup is with the amount of ice the main store does for me. I will stick to the main store near home depot

body.input: REVIEW TEXT The new owners have ruined this store, along with the one in sedro. I, who use to work at this store, know how subway is supposed to operate, and these owners do what they want. First, they added the old coolers so now you can’t see them put the meat and cheese on your sandwich. I have no way of knowing if they put enough meat or cheese on the sandwich until it gets to the veggie side, even that’s hard since it’s not really easy to count meat when it’s not folded. Subway is very picky on how sandwiches are made, the meat not being folded is a red flag because if they can’t do that what else are they doing wrong? The bread is always over cooked and dry, I believe it’s from the day before. The vegetable are always so sad and wilted. 6 months ago I saw them dump fresh tomato’s onto of old tomato’s. Even if they are from the same day the older batch always go on top. Finally, I ordered combos and I swear instead of putting them as combos he just put everything in the POS by themselves, making it more expensive. I will be reaching out to corporate and everyone else should do the same. They have no business running a subway.

REVIEW TEXT Update
Accidentally ordered a pick up order from here meaning to order from college way. Ordered through the website and asked for “less” mayo and mustard. There is so much the paper ripped opening it. This is a garbage $17 sandwich. Don’t order from here. Picture is from tonight’s sandwich. If I could give 0 stars I would.

Tried to order sandwiches tonight though doordash. We put the order in for a later delivery (an hour and a half after placing it). We received phone call from door dash letting us know that subway was out of bread. This is the third let down from this subway. The latest was an in person attempt when we showed up an hour and a half before closing time and they were closing and not making sandwiches anymore that evening. There were teenagers closing the subway and a bunch of other teens waiting for them at tables. Not to say it’s not staffing issues because I understand it’s still hard to staff restaurants well but man, I won’t make this mistake again. Buyer beware, choose the College Way subway over this one every time. 🤷‍♀️

body.input:
REVIEW TEXT There were some highlights and then some big misses, especially given the price point. Overall, I felt the price point was high for most menu items given the execution and/or portion size.
Strangely, no cocktail list. Even a spirits list would be helpful. However, the bartender made me a delicious aviation upon request. Wine list was limited in styles.
Pan fried oysters were hot and crispy with a rich house made sauce (Caesar?). Field greens were good with a variation on a Caesar dressing; just wish portion size was bigger for the price. Tartare was okay, but lacked seasoning. Raw oysters were clean and fresh (albeit pricey) with an interesting grapefruit granita instead of mignonette.
Husband had the scallops/risotto for his main and the dish was beautifully presented and scallops perfectly cooked. The risotto was unfortunately very under seasoned, a shame given how lovely the flavours were.
Our table mates had the cioppino, generous with seafood. Different style than a typical cioppino; less tomatoey. The toast served with it was burnt. They also had the filet, which was very thick and cooked perfectly rare. The steak and potatoes lacked salt and the dish as a whole really needs a sauce to tie it all together.
Dessert got weird. They served the crème brûlée on a plate with a square cutout of the menu. It tasted off to me, like sour milk, but the rest of the table seemed to like it. The chocolate mousse was served soft-serve style in a coffee cup without any further garnish. It was dense and tasted more like bland pudding. No dessert cocktails were offered.
In general, the service was lovely when the server was at our table. The servers were dressed professionally which I appreciated and added to the ambiance. I wish they had checked in more frequently as plates and finished food sat on our table for awhile, and I was never checked in with after I finished my first drink, so it was the only drink I ordered.
Wasn’t a terrible experience or anything like that but nothing was exceptional enough for me to warrant a return for the prices.

body.input: REVIEW TEXT Great indian place! We had Lamb Biriyani and some other lamb curry with coconut in it. Both tasted great. They ask you beforehand your intended spice level, and they know their spices. We took the maximum spice level and it was really spicy! Loved this! I personally preferred the curry more than the biriyani. We also had the Pakora Platter, that was quite average. But the Saffron Ice cream we had as dessert was really good! The place was quite nice overall, as well as the food. Recommended if you want to experience good spicy indian food.

body.input: REVIEW TEXT New favorite! We were warmly greeted upon entry, told we could sit wherever we like and there’s a water station. It was very clean and very well lit due to the natural lighting. Our server was the most attentive and considerate person. She gave us space but also made sure to see how we liked our first bites and that we had enough water and offered to package our leftovers at the end. We only kept leftovers so we had enough food for the next day too because it was so good we wanted to “keep the party going”. I highly recommend the mango lemonade and the vegetable and mango curry. It was very easy to eat vegan here. I highly recommend coming here!

body.input: REVIEW TEXT Sooo one of my gfs and I decided to head to a bar for  Martini after we just had a full day at the Tulalip festival and eating oysters. I don't live in the area so it's always a treat visiting. First time at this bar and I thought I looked fun. We were just in time for Happy Hour. I loved the waitress/bartender who helped us. Super friendly and it was cool my friend could bring her dog to sit outside (only) with us while we had our drinks. I decided on an Asian Pear martini and we ordered the artichoke dip. The dip was pretty good. I could've did without the cream cheese in it but the garlic bread that came with it was delicious. My drink was so good! I love the vibe here. I definitely will be back again whenever I'm in the area!

REVIEW TEXT IHOP was our fifth stop after a local power outage shut down most of the local spots.

I loved IHOP as a kid, but I was really disappointed with this visit. It wasn't the staff's fault in any way, they were attentive and helpful. It's just clear that IHOP has slipped from "beloved pancake spot" to "mid-level, crappy chain with gross, chemically-tasting food." And they had ZERO healthy options on the menu. The bright spot was the staff; they were amazing. The only issue here is corporate's push to homogenize their menu to the point that it's offensively gross.

body.input: REVIEW TEXT Had a burger and fries, both great. But I went for a European soccer game (UEFA women's). I prefer a artisanal beer, but I did not ask about bottled, because they had pFriem and Bodhizafa IPAs on tap. Both perfect while I watched an afternoon match. I'll be back. Lunch menu is a pretty good deal. Patron said the pizza was worth trying. Both the owner and the bartender very friendly. perfect neighborhood sports bar, with decent (8?) range of taps.

REVIEW TEXT Best place to play pool in Mount Vernon with tournaments on Mondays, Tuesdays, Thursdays, and Saturdays. The girls behind the bar are always running and providing excellent service. . One of my favorite establishments, I've been coming here since they had the bar in the main pool room. It's nice that they dedicated a space for the lounge and a separate room for the pool tables.

Draft Pic's is a Mount Vernon staple establishment, gathering place, pool hall, and otherwise great place to meet up with friends for drinks, games, karaoke, etc.

REVIEW TEXT I stopped by the Mount Vernon, WA Taco Bell yesterday afternoon and had a really solid experience. Ordered a couple of burritos (they were tasty and hit the spot) and a medium Dr Pepper. I took advantage of the 2–5 p.m. discount, which was nice, and also got 51% cash back (up to $10) through the Upside app—always love saving a few bucks.
The staff was lively, kind, and super friendly. Service was quick and everything came out hot and fresh. What really stood out was the manager (or owner?) walking in with a box and personally handing out little gifts to every employee right in front of me—it was a really thoughtful touch and made the whole place feel warm and positive.
Definitely a great quick stop. Solid food, great service, and a little holiday spirit. Will be back!

Nothing blew us away at EMDM. On to the next Mexican spot to try.

To management: DO NOT ACCEPT ONLINE ORDERS IF YOU CANNOT FULFILL THEM IN A TIMELY MANNER.

body.input:
REVIEW TEXT Dennys is a unique place in that the food is hit or miss and that's between menu items versus who is cooking. It's 24/7 which is great however that does draw a lot of crazy characters. I have really enjoyed the employees there, and met some great people. If you want a cheap meal the value menu can't be beat... especially since at 3am nobody is open. They have wifi if I recall. There are no customer available outlets, but there's a bathroom that's always clean and available when necessary.

I have gotten the value burger and fries, the value slam (basic breakfast) and I got the club sandwich with fries this last time. The value menu items are enough food for me so I shouldn't wander; however, I got the club. It was enormous. So much meat in it. I had a hard time squashing it down to fit in my mouth. I didn't finish a half and only 1/3 the fries. (Fries are always hot crispy and good) I took the other half to go but it barely fit in the container. I had to press down to get it to snap closed. Very good IMHO.  Thank you to the staff for your patience and good service.

BTW sometimes I go in to use the bathroom or just sit warm up and get some water and they don't complain, but they do know I'm a courteous customer. I'm sure they'd be like that to anyone if they are behaving and courteous.

REVIEW TEXT Amazing Food & Service

This place was an absolute gem! The food was incredible I ordered fried rice with extra teriyaki chicken on top (see photo), and it was packed with flavor, cooked perfectly, and portioned generously. The chicken was tender and juicy with just the right amount of glaze.

If you’re in Mt. Vernon and craving Asian comfort food, Orange Chicken should be your go-to. I’ll definitely be coming back!

REVIEW TEXT Nut allergy warning: Obviously, avoid the PB&J and probably let them know about any allergies.

I thought an affordable, quality sandwich shop didn't exist in the PNW. But when I went to go visit a friend in Mount Vernon, not only did I find a very reasonable one, but they have affordable matcha and coffee to boot? I would be a regular if I lived here, no doubt about it.

The pork belly sandwich (5/5): Rich, tender, juicy, the perfect filling amount for lunch.
Mochi cream donut (5/5): Take a Boston creme and eliminate the randomness you'd get from a dry pastry dough. Chewy, creamy, somewhat sharable since my sugar tolerance is low but it's not too sweet either.
My friend said his beef sandwich was a banger (no photo, he finished it too fast).

I was so lucky that they opened recently and I hope they continue this level of quality. Stop by on the drive through. Would recommend.

REVIEW TEXT As one of the well known fast food Asian chain restaurants, they didn't even bother to put up the price for their juice. Is it just an overlook, laziness or purely intentional? What kind of business practice is this, Panda Express???
This has been my favourite go-to place to get Asian fast food, I will NOT go there again.

body.input: REVIEW TEXT Every single time we go to this place it is a disaster. Any time we do not go inside the orders are wrong . One time I ordered fried rice with double orange chicken and they forgot the orange chicken. I opened my tray at home to only find rice. This last time they forgot a complete order for door dash . Ordered 2 entrees and only got 1 . Any time we go through the drive through they are out of almost every thing we order and we end up having to wait 5-15 minutes or they don’t offer a wait at all they just say they are plain out. Going inside is not a much better experience , last time we did that I was almost late to work because it took 20 minutes to get the orders for the 6 people in front of me . Then when they wanted to pay in cash the girl at the register did not know what to do with it and had to get management involved. I tried to ask if I could pay first and be on my way and they said no , they had already rang them up . Also just the quality of the food , the chicken is usually mushy and the rice and noodles are always dry , we have to pour soy sauce on them just to rehydrate it most of the time. We have been to many other locations including Arlington, Marysville and Everett. This is by far the worst Panda Express we have ever gone to. I think we have finally learned our lesson and won’t be giving them another chance to screw things up.

See you next time we're in town Skagit Valley Food Coop!

REVIEW TEXT I hadn’t been here in 15+ years, returning as an adult, I truly appreciate how fantastic it is! They carry anything and everything you could possibly want or need.

Produce is vibrant, local, organic, reasonably priced - it was hard not to buy everything!

Meat and deli department have great selections, like marinated meats, making dinner options easy.

They have a great selection of ready-made meals (lasagna, soup, wild salmon, samosas, and salads).

The bakery’s clearly a hit since by 1:00pm, many products had low-stock or were sold out, a sign of yummy treats! We shared a Raspberry Cream Cheese Turnover, it was decadent.

Exploring the isles, everything’s fairly priced compared to alternate grocers, and many items had promotions.

All staff we encountered were exceptionally friendly and welcoming!

They have a super cute cafe, serving coffee, tea, sundaes and smoothies. Take a seat by the window to people watch, or enjoy additional seating upstairs.

body.input:
REVIEW TEXT Just along College Way, at the intersection of N. LaVenture, you find yourself confronted with the titular ‘College.’ A founding ground for the community’s proud few—but when they want something to chew, where do they go? Across the street, one structure: a gas station–McDonald’s combination stands tall, ready to ease the hungers brought forth from so much learning. It’s a compact spot, occupying a busy corner with nimble traffic.

On the day you appear at the quick stand, you find the parking lot bustling. Forced to park at the very corner beside the sign for the establishment, you’re provided a tremendous view of the building and the sign.

McDonald’s and Chevron—a novel combination, one the locals reverently refer to as ‘McChevron.’ It’s a title embracing the fatal juxtaposition. Does one occupy the other? More restaurant or gas station? Is it some sort of comment on the nature of our needs and convenience being so at odds?

The site itself has acquired a renown for being the host to some tragedy—gas pumps transformed to headstones on the lawn of the venture promised to bring convenience.

But as you push your way through the two-door entry, you see a path through. The convenience market is a brief trail to McDonald’s seclusion, a small but long café space nestled away from the parking lot’s painful memories. The familiar trappings are there—mixed seating options willing to accommodate a litany of uses, screen with orders upon it, colorful imagery of items on offer. Your old friend, the Kiosk, sits smugly in the center of it all. It has a kind of “Didn’t think I’d see you here!” air about it, but it should know by now you are a professional. You’ll be taking your Big Mac on points you’ve accumulated from all your McDonald’s visits. The Kiosk almost cries as it accepts your points as currency. It’s a profound exchange, a rare moment to witness for the average diner: customer and restaurant locked in a never-ending dance of gratitude, resulting in a deluxe menu item being prepared and served for nothing but the recognition of 5,000 points of one’s loyalty. You smirk as you accept your receipt—like you’d ever return this!

You place your number at your table and can’t help but feel the palpable sense of tragedy creep upon your back. Sure, the hamburger would be free, but at what cost? Do the crew members remember the fallen while they pull your fries from the oil? Boxed up and shipped away on the plastic tray that heads your way in the hands of one—she’s older, but so kind. You can see it in her face: a manager or owner. She’s seen it all before, but she’s never seen you, with your free Big Mac. And she’s happy for you.

Then you notice the decorations. Fresh-cut flowers in glass vases with clean water. String lights dangle from the ceiling. All of this, you are certain, was her work. Who could know such dedication? Why bring it here? But the answer was obvious—Stevie Wonder’s “Sir Duke” thumps along peacefully in the background, as you begin to feel it all over. Not the oblique fear that you may be the next gunned down, but the marked resilience on display in the way this McDonald’s continues to march along. Never giving up. Those tragedies may come, but inside, we keep the flowers fresh, the faces friendly, and the food free (if you have enough points).

The lessons in life take many shapes and come from diverse places. College may not be for some, but the McChevron is for all. While you’re not a student anymore, you know you still have a lot to learn. Maybe this McDonald’s could teach you a thing or two.

REVIEW TEXT God’s given McDonald’s and possibly the best one in the continuous United States. You wouldn’t expect it given how it is connected to a gas station.

I’ve been here ten times the past few weeks and my order hasn’t been screwed up ONCE even with special requests. No onions? No onions. Light Sauce? You got it. No cheese on my McGriddle? Nothing to worry about. Espresso shot, whipped cream and chocolate drizzle? Its ALL there. Its genuinely unbelievable how they get it right each time.

Consumerism is an issue but the app is way too flawless not to use it. For some reason this location gives really decent deals. It makes ordering a breeze. I get there in a couple minutes from the College and the food is already on the counter. Their transition from breakfast to lunch also seems seamless

I normally don’t dine-in but the inside is really nice and clean quite possibly the cleanest fast food location I have ever been in. Ever.

It’s immaculate. McDonald’s as a corporation isn’t the greatest but this location is an absolute gem. My biggest thanks to everyone that works there I hope you all get a good raise in your near future.

Ordered a BLT. Stale and hard bread.
Potatoe cakes tasted like it was cooked in OLD grease/oil.
I would call that no longer trustworthy to eat there.
If you want $30+ plus dollars for something to eat at least make it worth a dollar okay.

The food is absolutely great, was hot, fresh and well made.
The presentation of our sandwiches were super well made!
The store was super clean!
The young lady at the counter was super nice and very knowledgeable. And very clean and presentable!
The manager was super nice!
I don't know anyone there anymore, but I plan on getting to know them and will be visiting often!
All of the "other" fast food places have totally turned us off with poor  food quality, and bad presentation of food.

REVIEW TEXT My son had a two-piece combo for $11.89 and I had a Famous Bowl combo for $8.99. body.input: REVIEW TEXT I placed a pickup order at KFC through the DoorDash app and started heading to the restaurant. I get there at the perfect time that it states it’s ready. Pull thru the drive through asking for my pickup order and they make me pull out front. All is fine until 8 min go buy and someone is walking my order to my car for me. I roll my window down and I’m handed two LARGE bags of food and the person walks away. My boyfriend and I look in the bags and it’s not our order at all, it was like a 5 person family’s order. My boyfriend brings the bagged food back inside and tells them it’s not our order. The employee then asks for our name and walks away. The employee comes back 5 min later and asks for the order name AGAIN! Then another 5 min later we get our correct order. We park and start to open our food. I noticed I was missing and item and mentioned it to our boyfriend as he was just pulling out his food. Then BAM! His box of food falls right through the bottom because it was not shut or secured properly and was done lazy. Chicken wings/crumbs are EVERYWHERE on his pants and my car seats/floors. At this point we are not happy and he takes pictures of what happened and goes inside the store to show them and get my missing item. My boyfriend starts explaining what happened to them and the employee interrupts him twice saying what is the exact item to remake AS HE IS EXPLAINING IT TO THEM. As my boyfriend is waiting for the remade food three employees are in the corner talking shit saying “I’m glad the food fell in your car” PS. He was polite when he went inside to explain what happened he was not rude in anyway he just wanted his food remade because it fell and the box wasn’t put together correctly. KFC in Mount Vernon, you suck! It’s not hard to be nice & apologies when a mistake happens. But also it makes sense why you 3 three works work there with the horrible attitude and personality you guys all have! You know who you are.

body.input: REVIEW TEXT I've been waiting to try Rachawadee for years. Every time I've popped in, it's been too crowded for my claustrophobic self. Today, we lucked out as there were only 2 people waiting in front of us(speaks to just how good this place is) I really appreciated the manager explaining the spice level business. My wife is a, bring all the heat all day, kind of gal where I'm more of a 2-3. She got an 8 star phad thai,I got a 1. She also got a 4 star tom kah and that was the best tom kah I've ever had anywhere. The phad thai was exceptional and the 1 star is no joke, easily a 3/5 at other restaurants. I loved the vibe, the cleanliness and atmosphere. The food is just beyond fantastic and I'll definitely be back, even if it needs to be take out 😂

body.input: REVIEW TEXT Bad service. It took 45 minutes for my order to be ready, more than 20 minutes longer than the confirmation email said it would. Also the pretzel crust we ordered was just regular pizza crust with some big salt on in. Not sure if that’s right since we’ve never had it before.

body.input: REVIEW TEXT This walk up burger and special comfort food joint is clean and welcoming. We ate the large hand battered onion rings, Hawaiian burger and grilled sourdough burger, a large MNT Dew and the marshmallow shake large.  The onion ring tastes like they are battered in donut batter it’s so delicious we had the homemade ranch dipping sauce. The burgers uniqueness was appreciated and the vegetables on them were fresh and the buns soft. The shake got me though. It was like drinking a liquid peep. It was absolutely delish. I also watched people order I noticed two things one not one person left without a milkshake and also 2 pregnant women and one with baby and 2 small kids all thought the food was good enough to drag themselves out of there cars to snag some grub. As a mother myself I feel that speaks volumes. Staff was kind, kitchen looked clean, food was delivered fast and hot.

REVIEW TEXT What happened to Bob's Burger?
I have been coming here over the span of 20 years. The last time I came here over a year ago I swore I wouldn't go back. We still never saw our waitress one time during our meal not one. By the time we were finished she comes by and asked is everything OK? I was like for real? You haven't done your job one time during our stay here. Then after she took our plates we waited and waited and waited some more for the check. I finally had to get up and ask for the check. Unbelievable will not ever give this restaurant my business again never again. Save your money go elsewhere. ​

body.input:
REVIEW TEXT Domino’s Mount Vernon, you had one job: cut the pizza. Instead, you delivered a masterclass in modern art.

We ordered three large pizzas. One was supposed to be square-cut for the kids. Instead, we got:

Pizza #1: Half of it was cut in two giant slabs, and the other half in three prehistoric dinosaur-sized slices. Whoever cut this was either stoned, inspired by Picasso, or both.

Pizza #2: Looked like a blindfolded ninja gave it a shot. Six massive slices that could’ve been used as canoe paddles.

Pizza #3: No words. Just chaos. I’m convinced the cutter sneezed mid-slice, shrugged, and said, “Good enough.”

The staff was fun and welcoming, and the pizza itself? Delicious. But the slicing had our whole family crying with laughter. Honestly, I’m not even mad… this was dinner and a comedy show rolled into one.

So yes, Mount Vernon Domino’s, the pizza was perfect. But next time, I’ll just ask for “uncut” and bring my own scissors, because clearly your slicer is living his best abstract-art life.

REVIEW TEXT 2024 Feb
Josh is great. Come on in and say hi to him
My handyman James Catway  makes perfect eggs and he said he learned it over at his aunt's place here at Bonnie Joe's and I have to agree. The eggs are fabulous here. I had the waffle, sausage and eggs

everything is just perfect and fast and super clean. Saw three people wiping tables, greeting customers, pouring coffee, setting up. No idle hands.

with Josh's excellent personal attention, he made sure I got the best coffee and cream.

It seems like a real family cozy place. They're calling out names of customers individually as they come in the door or leave. This is a nice place to be. I'm giving a five-star again  Another five star review so be sure to give Josh a shout out please.

2023
Wow this place was packed, had to get on waiting list on a Wednesday morning. With good reason.

Waffle was perfect, soft and mouthfeel for Belgium waffle with sugar free syrup available.

Denver omelet was exquisite. In other places they used old meat and too dry.

Exceeded expectations! Set bar to new high.

Krystal is awesome.
Lots of staff to refill coffee etc.

Also the old boys club of Bonnie Jo's had some walking sticks they reclaim and share.

We actually came to town from Rockport to replace my husband's walking stick so it came at opportune time.

Beautiful bathrooms indicate how clean kitchen is too.

REVIEW TEXT Very cute and sweet little spot! Only 2 stars for the food because it was very basic - ok. Actually I ordered the bkft sandwich (1 of the 2 bkft items avail) and it reminded me of the pkg bkft sandwiches you would get from Costco. When we travel, we seek out the little mom and pop shops for their unique, home made, locally sourced menu items. So, as you can imagine, i was disappointed. My hubby ordered the french toast, and that looked and smells good. So we had 2 of the 2 item on the bkft menu.

The atmosphere was pretty cool with the outdoor seating - some seats were in the sun and of course you could find shade under the umbrellas too! Cool place to chill, & hang out if your local, not too sure if would recommend it as a destination spot though.

The people were great! Maybe if we drive by it again we would give maybe the lunch menu  a try ....on a hot day. Oh, and the washroom was clean so 👌🏽

REVIEW TEXT Alvin Larsen is the fastest delivery driver on the force, nothing could stop him from delivering not even the group of pre-schoolers crossing the road.

Normally I don't like Domino's pizza but Alvin made sure my pizza was made with extra love mmmmmmm so yummy. When I said I couldn't afford a tip he gave me the extra cash in his wallet and said "pay it forward" so I used it to buy cigarettes and gave a dart to a homeless woman.

Alvin is a fantastic employee with passion for his craft, an unwaivering spirit, a light in the community, a humble young man who will stop at nothing to get the job done. I hope his boss recognizes all the work he does, his commitment has touched not only me but I'm sure everyone that has had the privilege of his presence has been touched deeply. Thank you for coming to my TED talk.
